classification.difficultyReason: Prove numerical and symbolic angle relationships using two parallel-line relationships and subtraction of adjacent angles.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 10, left cell, diagram beneath part a
spec.description: Narrow upright triangle AEF with C on AE, D on AF, B to the left of C on BCD, and BE completing parallelogram BDFE. Single parallel arrows match BE and DF; double parallel arrows match BD and EF.
spec.mathematics: A, C, E are collinear; A, D, F are collinear; B, C, D are collinear; BE is parallel to DF; BD is parallel to EF; angle ACD is 80 degrees and angle DFE is 70 degrees. Coordinates reproduce the schematic orientation without asserting lengths.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and structural markings are visible; no proof results appear.

answer.short: $\angle BEF=110^{\circ}$ (co-interior angles), $\angle CEF=80^{\circ}$ (corresponding angles). Hence $\angle BEC=110^{\circ}-80^{\circ}=30^{\circ}$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 10, right cell, diagram beneath part b
spec.description: Same upright configuration and relative scale as part a, with y at angle ACD and x at angle DFE. Preserve both parallel-marker families.
spec.mathematics: A, C, E are collinear; A, D, F are collinear; B, C, D are collinear; BE is parallel to DF; BD is parallel to EF; angle ACD is y and angle DFE is x.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and structural markings are visible; no symbolic proof results appear.

answer.short: $\angle BEF=180^{\circ}-x$ (co-interior angles add to $180^{\circ}$), $\angle CEF=y$ (corresponding angles). Hence $\angle BEC=(180^{\circ}-x)-y=180^{\circ}-(x+y)$.
